title: Fix `OS_LinuxBSD::get_video_adapter_driver_info()`: get IDs from currently selected graphics card

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
TODOs
* [x] get driver name
* [x] implement for compatibility mode
  * [x] stop crashing when calling this func
  * see `godot/drivers/gles3/storage/utilities.cpp`, change implementation to be analogous to `get_maximum_viewport_size` to avoid crash
  * update: calling `clGetDeviceInfo` with `CL_DEVICE_VENDOR_ID` as info should return the vendor id, and the device id is in `basisu::ocl::get_device_id()` in file `encoder/basisu_opencl.cpp`, but it's not accessible. re-doing the steps (see ´clGetDeviceIDs`) should provide the device ID
    * ~~for now, I'll bring back and improve the previous logic for gles3 as a fallback~~
    * getting driver name: improve guesswork in case of multiple cards
      * _or_ use `glxinfo -B` and read the lines  `Vendor:` and `Device:`, they contain the device IDs (dunno what `glxinfo` spits out when there are multiple cards
    * getting the version: `uname -r` (**6.14.0-35-generic**) + the result of using `glxinfo` (**Mesa 25.0.7**): `6.14.0-35-generic | Mesa 25.0.7`
      * steps: `glxinfo -B | grep "OpenGL renderer string"` returns `Mesa Intel(R) Arc(tm) Graphics (MTL)`. String splitting based on vendor name is too risky (because they are never consistent), so we take our chances and split on the first space. And by using `$ glxinfo -B | grep "Version"` we get the rest: `25.0.7`

* `modinfo` does not provide driver version
  * not sure if fixable. might be a limitation on some GPUs/drivers
    * known affected systems
      *  `Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS 24.04 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Arc(tm) Graphics (MTL) (i915)`
  * proposal: use `glxinfo` as seen above

fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112788
